references.text: Israel is described as God's treasured people and a holy nation, which connects to the idea that God loves his people and keeps his holy ones in his hand.
The Lord preserves his holy ones, reflecting Deuteronomy's description that all his holy ones are in his hand.
God's protection over believers, with the image of them being carried and kept at his feet.
Peoples come to the Lord's mountain to learn his ways and walk on his paths; they receive instruction from him.
Receiving words from God and staying close to him connects to the image of sitting at his feet and receiving his teaching.
Jesus speaks that no one can snatch his sheep out of his hand or the Father's hand, reflecting the image of the holy ones being secure in God's hand.
Mary sat at Jesus' feet and listened to his words, an image of discipleship connected to receiving instruction at the master's feet.
Paul describes how he was trained at Gamaliel's feet, a parallel to the image of sitting at the feet and receiving teaching.
